newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet trade stilled by tumbling futures.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet trade stilled by tumbling futures.

text.p: North Sea physical crude markets were deathly quiet on Thursday as traders stood back to watch outright prices tumble.
August Brent shed 71 cents on the IPE to close at $18.17 a barrel as futures traders collected profits, after four days of gains, before the Independence Day holiday in the United States.
On the physical market, thin supply was matched by unenthusiastic demand after refining margins were hit heavily this week by rising Brent prices.
Buyers were yet to react to Thursday's slump, dealers said.
"Obviously margins are now looking a lot better, but buyers don't see the need to rush back...they'll wait for things to settle down," said one.
The only reported physical deal was an Ekofisk, the best supplied of all the North Sea grades.
A cross-month cargo traded at a weaker Dated Brent +16 cents.
Two July 18-20 Brents turned wet on Thursday, one was kept by the equity holder and the other heard clocked to Shell UK.

Brent intermonth spreads came under pressure as the outright price fell. August/September fell some five cents from early talk to trade at -9 cents late in the day. September/October was talked at -15/-12.
CFDs also slipped with July 14-18 traded at September -18 cents and July 28-August 1 traded at September -28 cents. Next week (July 7-11) talked at August +3/+5 in late discussion.
Supply tightness continued to support Mediterranean sour markets, with one of the three remaining large July Urals cargoes on offer at a firm Dated Brent -60 cents.
But refiners were still complaining of poor margins and buying interest was thin.
One Sicilian refiner was heard to have cut back crude runs.
"They are trimming runs at any opportunity. They are cutting back in various parts of the plant and optimising output," said a source familiar with the refinery's operations.
